coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: 60–75 minutes easy Z2, rolling terrain, 800–1200 ft vert. Your RHR is down to 56 (8.7 bpm below your 30-day average) and recovery score is 92—you're in an ideal taper window. This isn't a maintenance run; it's a neural sharpener. Keep it aerobic (130–140 bpm ballpark), hit some short climbs to remind your legs and nervous system what's coming in 6 days, but finish feeling fresher than you started. No threshold work, no long pushes. You've banked the fitness; now you're priming the engine.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat 60–80g carbs with this run (you're still logging heavy Z2 volume relative to rest days). Post-run, get 20–30g protein + 80–120g carbs within 90 minutes to anchor glycogen while taper is active. You've had 8.3h of solid sleep—use that recovery window aggressively. Given the sparse aid stations in the Julian Alps (you'll be self-sufficient for long stretches), practice your race-day nutrition bottle setup on tomorrow's or Monday's easy run if you haven't already. Dial in exactly what you'll carry and how you'll pace your intake over 7+ hours.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your biggest lever in the final 6 days—you're already crushing it at 8.3h with 88.8% efficiency. Protect that. No late meetings, no red-eye flights this week if you can help it; you've got a race in Slovenia that demands 2,500m of vert and your windows for quality sleep are finite. RHR dip and high recovery score confirm your body is ready to absorb sharp work. Use this Saturday and Sunday to stay horizontal as much as possible between runs. No strength work, no long walks. Rest is the third pillar of taper, after volume reduction and intensity retention.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 6 days out and your physiology is primed—resting HR at 56, recovery score at 92, sleep quality elite. The race is won or lost now between your ears. Spend today's run getting familiar with effort cues: what 50K pace (likely 7:30–8:15/mi depending on vert) feels like on rolling terrain, how your breathing settles on the climbs, where your focus needs to be. Visualize the Kranjska Gora environment—alpine weather, technical descent sections, sparse aid—and see yourself moving efficiently through it. You don't need confidence; you need clarity. Execute the plan.
